name: Regions Financial

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Regions Financial is a Birmingham-based bank holding company ($163B assets, 1,246 branches) that takes deposits and lends to consumers and businesses across the South, Midwest and Texas, and also sells wealth, treasury and capital-markets services. Money model explained in two sentences.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Three segments (Consumer Bank, Corporate Bank, Wealth Management). Q3 revenue $1,973M: net interest income $1,298M (66%), fees $675M (34%): service charges $171M, wealth $146M, card $126M, capital markets $107M, mortgage $32M. Segment revenue split not extracted; deposit split by segment used instead.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Loans $99.8B: business 68% (C&I $52.4B, investor real estate $10.2B, owner-occupied CRE $5.4B), consumer 32% (home mortgage $19.4B, home equity $5.5B). Deposits $129.5B: consumer $81.0B, corporate $39.3B, wealth $7.4B. No single-customer concentration disclosed; investor real estate is 44% multifamily, 7% data centers, 6% office.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: All US, no FX exposure. 1,247 branches at year-end 2025: Florida 270, Tennessee 194, Alabama 184, Georgia 117, Mississippi 97, Texas 85, Louisiana 79. 10-K names concentration in the South, Midwest and Texas as a risk.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread bank: net interest margin 3.68% (Q3), NII $1,298M. Non-interest-bearing deposits $40.8B are 31% of deposits; total deposit cost 1.17% (1.39% a year earlier). Loans/deposits 77.1%. Fees 34% of revenue add a second stream. Not a stronghold like JPM: fee mix is mid-size.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Efficiency ratio 56.2% (adj. 55.8%); FY26 adjusted expense guided +1.5-3.5% against NII +2.5-4%, aiming for positive operating leverage. Guidance record: NCO guide 40-50bp 'toward the lower end', fee income guide 3-5% 'toward the lower end' (a trim). Bank: no inventory or working-capital cycle; branch network and technology build are the fixed-cost base.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs are deposits ($129.5B; consumer $81.0B; corporate $39.3B; wholesale/brokered 'other' only $1.8B), wholesale funding (short-term borrowings $4.5B, long-term $6.0B, up from $0.75B and $4.1B at year-end 2025) and capital (CET1 10.8%). Suppliers are local households and firms: no concentrated supplier; one soft spot is a few large commercial clients moving balances off balance sheet (~$16B held in off-balance-sheet products). FHLB availability fell to $6.9B from $10.2B a year ago; total liquidity $64B, ~170% of uninsured deposits. Pass-through: management expects a terminal rising-rate deposit beta in the mid/high 30s%; interest-bearing deposit cost 1.70% (+1bp QoQ, -31bp YoY) vs peers +2-3bp QoQ. Asset side reprices: new fixed-rate asset yields ~100bp above maturing; but NII +200bp gradual adds only $67M because of hedges. Signal tags: fed_funds, 2y, real_spending, hy_spreads (industry map).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Low-cost sticky deposits: total deposit cost 1.17% and 31% non-interest-bearing; a net asset-swap hedge book ($18.9B net) mutes rate swings; record Treasury Management and capital-markets revenue. New: building a cloud deposit platform, bought Frazier Lanier (July 2026). Company says it has the best return on tangible equity in its peer group five years running (company claim, own peer set; not independently checked).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Regional bank brand, #1 in regional-bank website satisfaction in 6 of 7 years (J.D. Power, company-cited), 1,246 branches, 2.75M mobile users. Would customers notice if gone: locally yes, nationally no. Marketing $29M a quarter, about 1.5% of revenue.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: JPM, BAC, WFC, Truist, Truist, Fifth Third, Synovus, Hancock Whitney. Ending loans +3.9% YoY vs US bank loans +8.9% annualised in October (H.8, per industry map); total deposits -0.6% YoY. Consumer deposits +1.6% YoY. Looks like share loss on loans, but FDIC market-share data not pulled.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Guidance is modest: FY26 average loans and deposits up low single digits, NII +2.5-4%. Pipelines +19% YoY, commitments +6%; new commercial logos +34% YTD; Q4 NIM guided ~3.70%; AFS securities AOCI of $1.9B burns down to $1.2B by YE2028 (capital release). Fixed-rate asset repricing helps NII, but this is already in guidance.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: Reported return on average tangible equity 21.3% (adj. 21.7%), but the denominator is cut by $3.2B of AOCI losses; my estimate excluding AOCI ~17.5% (annualised Q3 net income to common $2,444M / ~$13.95B); 2025 adjusted ROATCE ex-AOCI was 15.4% (proxy). CET1 10.8% vs 9.25-9.75% operating range. Buybacks: 19M shares for $555M YTD (avg ~$29), share count 885M to 850M in a year (-4%); dividend raised 13% to $0.30; payout 41.8%. Insiders: no open-market purchases in 2026; four small Form 4 sales (largest 36,000 shares at $28.78 on 2026-01-26). Pay: long-term awards are 64% of CEO target pay, tied to adjusted ROATCE ex-AOCI. CFO changed Mar 2026; CAO retires Jan 2027.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Deposit-funded lending is essential and not being displaced; relevance risk is slow (stablecoins and fintech deposit competition, named in risk factors). Not gaining relevance either: deposits -0.6% YoY. Key-person: CEO Turner (Chairman, President, CEO); two senior officers changed in 2026 (new CFO from inside; CAO retiring).

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: EY clean opinion; sole critical audit matter is the loan-loss allowance; no 8-K Item 4.01/4.02, no NT filing, no CORRESP/UPLOAD letters in the recent filing list; disclosure controls effective. Minor: recurring securities-repositioning losses ($15M Q3, $40M Q2), adj. vs GAAP EPS gap small ($0.73 vs $0.71), legal settlement costs raised professional fees $7M QoQ. Portfolios of interest: business offices ($773M, $134M non-performing) and trucking.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Built to be neutral: gradual +200bp adds only $67M of NII over 12 months (about 1.3%), -100bp costs $52M. So a Fed hike helps little. Boom +: loan growth and fees. Overheat 0: hedged, deposits reprice at mid/high-30s beta. Stagflation -: credit and funding costs. Slowdown 0: credit loss risk (NCO 29bp now, 40-50bp FY guide), but falling long yields repair $3.2B AOCI.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Basel III endgame expected to put AOCI into capital but cut risk weights: estimated pro-forma CET1 ~10% vs 9.25-9.75% range. No pending deal, docket or enforcement item found; legal contingencies are routine per 10-Q note 12.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $27.78 (2026-11-25) / tangible book $12.65 = 2.20x. Ex-AOCI tangible book $16.41: 1.69x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth, 1.69x (ex-AOCI) implies ROTCE ~14.8% (0% growth: 16.9%); 2.20x on AOCI-inclusive book implies 18.4%. Actual: ~17.5% ex-AOCI (my estimate), 21.3% reported. Cushion ~2.7 points, thin at 0% growth. P/E 10.9x trailing GAAP EPS $2.55 (9.8x annualised Q3 $0.71); dividend yield 4.3%. Own year-end 2025 P/TBV 1.91x ($26.32/$13.75), so it has re-rated up; 5-year range not extracted. Peers (sibling files): HBAN 1.57x, TFC 1.50x, WFC 1.82x, USB 2.00x (1.65x ex-AOCI), PNC 2.05x. RF is priced at the top of the regionals. 52-week range $24.72-$32.47.

status_reason: Quality B and credit improving, but the price (2.20x tangible book, top of the regional peer group) already pays for a ~17-18% return on tangible equity and rate sensitivity is hedged to neutral, so there is no identifiable mistake.
answer_to_lead_question: Is the deposit franchise worth more in a hiking regime than the price says? No evidence of that. Deposit costs are low (total 1.17%, down 22bp YoY, interest-bearing +1bp QoQ vs peers +2-3bp) but management hedged to a neutral rate position: +200bp gradual adds only $67M of NII, and it expects a mid/high-30s% terminal beta, not a low one. The margin advantage already shows in NIM 3.68% and the price has re-rated from 1.91x to 2.20x tangible book since year-end 2025. Possible upside not yet a mistake: $3.2B AOCI losses accrete back over time (to $1.2B by YE2028) and Basel endgame lifts CET1 to ~10%, both disclosed by the company.

feedback.fact: Regions says rising interest rates in Q3 raised unrealized securities losses: AOCI loss widened to $3,197M from $1,922M; tangible book/share fell to $12.65 from $13.78 in one quarter.
feedback.effect: confirms long yields rose through Q3 (consistent with 10y peak 5.07%); a Slowdown turn with falling long yields would reverse it

feedback.fact: Management says client sentiment is constructive, consumer credit fundamentals are healthy, employment conditions supportive, and consumer spending patterns consistent with recent trends; commercial pipelines +19% YoY.
feedback.effect: contradicts a near-term Slowdown in this bank's customer base through September; matches the hard-data Overheat read, not the credit-spread signal

feedback.fact: 4Q26 guidance (NII +1-2%, NIM ~3.70%) assumes a December Fed hike and stable long rates.
feedback.effect: confirms a December hike is the base case in bank planning; hedges make the NII effect small

feedback.fact: Total deposit cost 1.17% (1.18% Q2, 1.39% a year ago); interest-bearing 1.70% (+1bp QoQ).
feedback.effect: deposit-cost drift is smaller than the +2-3bp at TFC, HBAN, KEY, COF in the industry map (definitions may differ); supports low-beta franchise, but it is already in the margin

coverage_notes.10-K: FY2025 10-K read selectively: auditor opinion, critical audit matter, business/branches, deposits by segment. Segment revenue table and risk-factor text not read in full.
coverage_notes.10-Q: Q3 2026 10-Q read selectively (rate-sensitivity table 19, portfolios of interest, investor real estate, buybacks, legal note). Other three quarters used via the 5-quarter trend in the Q3 financial supplement, not the filings.
coverage_notes.presentation: Q3 deck is EX-99.3 on EDGAR; text extracted, chart images not read, so some chart values (hedge book detail) come from text only.
coverage_notes.ir_fact_sheet: Quarterly financial supplement (EX-99.2) covered; separate ir.regions.com fact sheet not fetched.
coverage_notes.def14a: 2026 proxy searched for pay mix, LTIP metric and pay-versus-performance table; ownership table and director holdings not read; insider trades checked directly through Form 4 XML (63 Form 4s filed in 2026).
coverage_notes.red_flag_scan: EDGAR submissions list scanned 2023-11 to 2026-11: no 8-K Items 4.01/4.02, no NT 10-K/10-Q, no CORRESP/UPLOAD; Item 5.02 on 2026-01-12 (CFO change) and 2026-08-11 (CAO retiring).
coverage_notes.price: yFinance last close 2026-11-25 $27.78; shares 848.8M. Own 5-year P/TBV not extracted (preferred and share count XBRL missing for earlier years); only year-end 2025 computed from the release. Peer multiples taken from sibling triage files, not recomputed.
coverage_notes.deposit_beta: No cumulative beta published for the cycle; only the forward 'terminal rising-rate beta mid/high 30s%'. I did not compute a historical beta.
coverage_notes.peer_deposit_cost: Industry map labels HBAN/TFC/KEY figures as cost of total deposits, which may mean interest-bearing; RF total 1.17% vs interest-bearing 1.70%. Direct peer ranking is unverified.
